header.running_head: The Marriages of Rasulullaah ﷺ and the Sahabah (RA)

blocks.text: away, Rasulullaah ﷺ was still living in Makkah. It was then that Hadhrat Khowla bint Hakeem bin Awqas (RA) the wife of Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Madh'oon (RA) suggested, "O Rasulullaah ﷺ! Are you not interested in getting married?" "To whom?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. She replied, "A virgin if you wish or a previously married woman if you wish." "Who is the virgin?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. Hadhrat Khowlah (RA) replied, "She is the daughter of the person you like best, Aa'isha the daughter of Abu Bakr (RA)." "And who is the previously married woman?" Rasulullaah ﷺ asked. "She is Saudah bint Zam'ah (RA)," came the reply, "she has believed in you (as Allaah's Rasul) and follows you in your Deen." Rasulullaah ﷺ then said to her, "Go and mention my name to them."

Hadhrat Khowlah (RA) went to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)'s house where she found Hadhrat Ummu Roomaan (RA) who was the mother of Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA). "O Ummu Roomaan," she said, "What tremendous goodness and blessings is Allaah about to shower on your family! Rasulullaah ﷺ has sent me to propose for Aa'isha's hand in marriage." Hadhrat Ummu Roomaan said, "I would love it, but let us wait for Abu Bakr who is soon to arrive." When he came, Hadhrat Khowlah (RA) said to him, "What tremendous goodness and blessings is Allaah about to shower on your family! Rasulullaah ﷺ has sent me to propose for Aa'isha's hand in marriage." Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) asked, "Is she suitable for him? She is the daughter of his brother."

Hadhrat Khowlah (RA) reported back to Rasulullaah ﷺ the doubt that Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) expressed. Rasulullaah ﷺ said, "Go back and tell him that he is my brother in Islaam and that I am his brother in Islaam (not by blood). His daughter is therefore suitable for me." When she conveyed the message to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA), he said, "Call Rasulullaah ﷺ here." Rasulullaah ﷺ then came and Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) got Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) married to him. [^1]

Another narration states at the end that Rasulullaah ﷺ told Hadhrat Khowlah (RA), "Go back and tell him that I am his brother in Islaam (not by blood) and that he is my brother in Islaam. His daughter is therefore suitable for me." When Hadhrat Khowlah (RA) returned with the message, Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) told her to wait and then left the house. Hadhrat Ummu Roomaan (RA) says that Mut'im bin Adi had requested the hand of Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) for his son Jubayr and Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) had promised it to him. Because Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) never broke a promise, he went to see Mut'im. With Mut'im at the time was his wife who was the mother of the boy in question (Jubayr). She however spoke to Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) in such harsh terms that the desire to fulfil his promise to Mut'im was forced out of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA)'s heart.
Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) asked Mut'im, "What have you to say about this girl (my daughter? Are you still interested in getting your son married to her)?"
Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.225) has commented on the chain of narrators.
